It actually does, but the tests are assuming that runfiles tree path == exec root path, which is no longer true.  You can't use $location to get the runfiles tree path.

Which means that pattern is no longer valid:
https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/tools/cpp/test/BUILD#L74 Which should be, shouldn't it?

Other skylark rules are failing because the path they are getting is an execroot dependent path.
How far are we from getting the deep_execroot turn on by default? Maybe we should stay in the intermediary state until we can get the deep execroot turned on (or maybe we can turn on now in Bazel but not internally).

deep execroot is on by default (and has been for several weeks), but that doesn't mean the exec root paths have been rearranged yet (that's the hard part).  That change will hopefully go out for code review this week.

issue.title: Use short_path for runfiles paths
issue.body:
_java.path was (incidentally) working, but is now broken. short_path is
for paths relative to the runfiles tree.

This fixes ci.bazel.io's rules_closure project. See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/1316 for more info.
